subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: Should OpenClaw forbid assistant, cron, or exec-originated CLI config writes to exec/sandbox settings without explicit operator approval, and should assistant-visible sandbox errors drop config-setting hints?
rationale: The remaining issue crosses persistent config mutation authority, host exec capability, sandbox posture, and plugin cron behavior; automation cannot safely choose the permanent trust boundary or operator UX policy.

options.title: Harden model-visible and exec-originated config writes
options.body: Remove protected config assignments from assistant-visible errors and add an explicit operator/provenance guard for CLI-through-exec or plugin/cron writes to exec and sandbox config.

options.title: Text-only mitigation
options.body: Only remove the remaining assistant-visible hints and leave CLI-through-exec config mutation policy unchanged for trusted high-power workflows.

options.title: Accept current trust model
options.body: Keep current config write semantics and close only if maintainers decide host-exec-capable agents are intentionally allowed to apply these config changes.

recommendation.title: Harden model-visible and exec-originated config writes
recommendation.body: Remove protected config assignments from assistant-visible errors and add an explicit operator/provenance guard for CLI-through-exec or plugin/cron writes to exec and sandbox config.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent work on the sandbox policy formatter and gateway config-tool boundary that are central to the decision.
